The '''2004–05 Scottish Premier League''' was won by [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], who claimed the title on the final day of the season by a single point from [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], who had gone into the final fixtures leading and were still ahead in the closing minutes of their last game against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] until they conceded two goals (both scored by striker [[Scott McDonald]]),<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/4565659.stm Motherwell 2-1 Celtic], BBC Sport, 22 May 2005</ref> costing them the title with Rangers winning their match against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in [[Edinburgh]].<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/4565709.stm Hibernian 0-1 Rangers], BBC Sport, 21 May 2005</ref> The dramatic events became known in popular culture as 'Helicopter Sunday' due to the aircraft ceremonially delivering the championship trophy changing direction in mid-flight as the identity of its winners altered suddenly.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32838481 Helicopter Sunday: Rangers' last-gasp triumph, 15 years on], BBC Sport, 21 May 2020</ref>

As league [[champions]], Rangers qualified for the UEFA Champions League group stage, with [[runner-up|runners-up]] [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] also qualifying to the third qualifying round. Third-placed [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] qualified for the [[UEFA Cup]], as did [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], who took the [[Scottish Cup]] place despite losing the final to Celtic.

[[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] were relegated, and [[Scottish First Division]] winners [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] were promoted.

[[John Hartson]] was the top scorer with 25 goals for Celtic, whose manager [[Martin O'Neill]] stepped down at the end of the season after five years and a host of major trophies.
